items.followUp: What is the purpose of the <b> tag in HTML?

rubric.why: The purpose of the font tag includes setting the font type or style.
rubric.description: States that the font tag changes the font face or style.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the font type or style as something the tag can change.

rubric.why: The font tag can also set text size and color.
rubric.description: States that the font tag can change the text size or color.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying size or color.

modelAnswer: The <font> tag is used to change the appearance of text on a web page.
It can set the font face, size, and color.

items.followUp: Which HTML tag is used to create an ordered list?

rubric.why: The <ul> tag creates an unordered list.
rubric.description: Names the correct unordered-list tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing <ul>.

rubric.why: An unordered list displays its items with bullets rather than a numbered sequence.
rubric.description: Identifies the list as a bulleted or unordered list.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it creates a bulleted/unordered list.

modelAnswer: Use the <ul> tag to create an unordered list in HTML.
Its list items are written inside <li> tags and are usually displayed with bullets.

items.followUp: Define a flowchart and explain how it helps in solving a problem.

rubric.why: An algorithm is a finite, ordered set of instructions for solving a problem.
rubric.description: Defines an algorithm as a step-by-step sequence of instructions.
rubric.how: Award up to 2 marks for identifying instructions/steps and their ordered or finite nature.

rubric.why: An algorithm provides a clear plan for reaching a solution.
rubric.description: Explains that an algorithm gives a clear plan for solving a problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its role as a solution plan or method.

rubric.why: A well-ordered algorithm helps a solver check the process and implement it as a program.
rubric.description: Explains a further role, such as checking the steps or guiding program implementation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant additional role.

modelAnswer: An algorithm is a finite, ordered sequence of clear steps or instructions for solving a problem.
It provides a logical plan that helps break a problem into manageable steps and reach a solution.
The steps can be checked for errors and then used to write a computer program.

items.followUp: Name the four TCP/IP layers and state one function of each.

rubric.why: The application layer provides network services to user applications.
rubric.description: Names the application layer and gives a relevant function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the layer with its function.

rubric.why: The transport layer manages end-to-end data delivery, including segmentation and reliability.
rubric.description: Names the transport layer and gives a relevant function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the layer with its function.

rubric.why: The Internet layer uses IP addressing and routes packets between networks.
rubric.description: Names the Internet layer and gives a relevant function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the layer with its function.

rubric.why: The network access layer handles sending data over the local network medium.
rubric.description: Names the network access layer and gives a relevant function.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the layer with its function.

modelAnswer: Application layer: Provides network services to applications, such as web and email services.
Transport layer: Provides end-to-end communication and may divide data into segments and support reliable delivery.
Internet layer: Uses IP addressing and routes packets between networks.
Network access layer: Sends data over the connected network medium, including handling frames and physical transmission.

items.followUp: Name four practices that can help protect a computer system from security threats.

rubric.why: Accessing a system or information without permission is an ethical security issue.
rubric.description: Identifies unauthorized access or hacking.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this issue.

rubric.why: Taking private or confidential data without permission is a security-related ethical issue.
rubric.description: Identifies theft of data or information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this issue.

rubric.why: Creating or spreading harmful software can damage systems and compromise security.
rubric.description: Identifies malware or viruses as a security issue.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this issue.

rubric.why: Misusing or exposing someone's personal information violates privacy.
rubric.description: Identifies violation of privacy or misuse of personal information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this issue.

modelAnswer: Unauthorized access or hacking into another person's system.
Stealing data or confidential information.
Creating or spreading malware such as viruses.
Violating privacy by misusing or exposing personal information.

items.followUp: What is a prototype, and how can it help when developing a solution?

rubric.why: A prototype is an early or preliminary model of a product or solution.
rubric.description: Defines a prototype as an early model.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this definition.

rubric.why: A prototype lets people test an idea, find problems, and improve the design before making the final version.
rubric.description: Explains a purpose of a prototype, such as testing, gathering feedback, or finding flaws.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant purpose.

modelAnswer: A prototype is an early model or sample version of a product or solution.
It is used to test an idea, find problems, and make improvements before producing the final version.

items.followUp: Describe how the “work backwards” problem-solving strategy is used.

rubric.why: Act it out is a problem-solving strategy in which the situation is performed or represented.
rubric.description: Identifies acting out or role-playing the situation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the strategy as performing or representing the situation.

rubric.why: Acting out helps make the problem clearer and can reveal a way to solve it.
rubric.description: States that the strategy helps understand or solve the problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant purpose.

modelAnswer: “Act it out” is a problem-solving strategy in which the situation is physically performed or represented.
It helps make the problem easier to understand and can reveal a possible solution.

items.followUp: Name two symbols used in a flowchart and state what each represents.

rubric.why: An oval or terminator symbol represents the start or end of a flowchart.
rubric.description: Names a valid flowchart symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one correct symbol, such as an oval (terminator).

rubric.why: A diamond, rectangle, or parallelogram is another standard flowchart symbol.
rubric.description: Names a second valid flowchart symbol.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a different correct symbol.

modelAnswer: Oval (terminator): represents the start or end of a flowchart.
Diamond: represents a decision or condition.
